speaker: Doctor
text: What is the primary complaint that brought you to the clinic today, and how long has this been happening?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of levofloxacin use is concerning for antibiotic-associated diarrhea, possibly *Clostridioides difficile*. Have you noticed any blood or mucus in the stool, or do you have a high fever? REQUEST TEST: C. diff toxin assay, Complete Blood Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C. diff toxin assay: Not specified; Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 13 g/dL, Total_Count_WBC 13,400/mm3, Differential_Count Neutrophils 80%, Lymphocytes 15%, Monocytes 5%

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile infection.
